transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-09-10
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jared Lowe (Highland), Priya Rao (Highland), Elena Martínez (Highland)

Auto-generated topics (may be partial): egress, private endpoints, transit gateway, SOC 2, KMS, SAML, dedicated vs hosted

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick intros, i'm maya, account lead for this region for redwood inference - and with me is samir our solutions eng — samir, quick wave?
[00:09] Samir (Redwood SE): hey hi, good to meet you all. i'll try to keep the technical bits succinct but happy to dive deep.
[00:15] Jared (Highland): thanks maya. today we want to validate that private deployment options meet our egress and data residency requirements. we run sensitive PII, must keep tokenized logs in eu region.
[00:26] Priya (Highland): also security wants to lock down egress, we can't have open internet egress from inference nodes, and we need allowlist IPs or use VPC endpoints.
[00:36] Elena (Highland): and latency is a factor — we have some interactive apps, target p95 under 200ms. cost matters but security is top.
[00:46] Maya: got it. high-level — redwood offers hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private (vpc / on-prem). for strict egress and zero public ingress, Private is usually the fit: private control plane + private endpoints. but dedicated in a customer VPC with private endpoints can work too depending on constraints.
[01:05] Samir: quick nuance — when people say "private endpoints" we mean things like aws privatelink / interface endpoints or azure private endpoints. we can also use transit gateway peering if you need centralized egress.
[01:19] Jared: we use TGW + centralized NAT gateway in eu-west-1. we'd prefer no cross-region hops. can your private deployment live in eu-west-1 only?
[01:29] Samir: yes, we can pin to eu-west-1 for the private control plane and inference nodes. one caveat: depending on model versions and fallback policies, occasionally model artifacts are pulled from other mirrors — but we can ensure those are mirrored in region.
[01:44] Priya: how about keys — KMS integration? our policy requires CMKs in our account and HSM-backed keys for any token logs.
[01:53] Maya: we support customer-managed KMS for Private; we can integrate with your KMS/HSM; for hosted we have bring-your-key options but private gives the best separation.
[02:03] Elena: and SSO — SAML and SCIM for provisioning?
[02:07] Samir: yes SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning are available; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. quick note: our audit log retention varies by tier; long-retention is an add-on.
[02:20] Maya: i'll share the security pack link after the call — note the docs sometimes show our product name as "Redwood Dedicatedy" in auto-transcripts, so ignore typos. link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (drive link, internal placeholder)
[02:35] Jared: thanks. on network egress controls: can you support IP allowlist for outbound requests from models (e.g., to external APIs)? we need to ensure models can't call out to arbitrary endpoints.
[02:47] Samir: two approaches: 1) restrict outbound at the VPC level in your account (NACLs, route to NAT with proxy), 2) we can enforce egress policies in the runtime to disallow external calls — runtime-level egress filtering is in our roadmap and partial today. for the pilot we recommend network-level controls.
[03:07] Priya: do you provide interface endpoints (PrivateLink) that map to the redwood control plane, or do we need to run a connector?
[03:14] Samir: for Private we provision interface endpoints in your VPC that map to our private control plane — they're region-local. for Dedicated sometimes we use cross-account peering or shared VPC patterns.
[03:24] Elena: what about peering limits and lifecycle? our infra team doesn't want long-lived cross-account peering due to blast radius.
[03:32] Samir: we can do a cross-account interface via aws privatelink which reduces peering footprint; for large deployments Transit Gateway peering is common. we also support ExpressRoute/DirectConnect if you're on-prem connected.
[03:46] Maya: question for Highland: are you planning a full pilot or a small POC? what's the timeline?
[03:52] Jared: we want a pilot for a chat/qa flow with 1-2 models, target in 6 weeks, low-risk; success metrics: data never leaves eu region, SSO provisioned, and p95 latency < 200ms under expected QPS.
[04:05] Priya: also need to validate egress allowlist and KMS integration before prod.
[04:10] Samir: ok on benchmarks — we can run a traffic profile against eu-west-1 nodes. quick baseline: egress via TGW + NAT can add 10-30ms depending. model tokenization and kv cache hit rates also affect p95.
[04:23] Jared: can you explain kv cache and prefix caching? will that change the network egress pattern?
[04:28] Samir: KV cache stores recent seqs in-memory on the serving node — so cache hits avoid re-computation and reduce compute time but still use local network for model shards. prefix caching helps for repeated prompts and will significantly reduce token costs. neither requires external egress unless you use external tool plugins.
[04:46] Elena: about plugins — we will not enable external tool calls. model must be sandboxed.
[04:50] Maya: noted. we'll ensure the deployment config disables tool calling and external connectors.
[04:56] Priya: any special firewall rules needed for the private endpoints? specific ports?
[05:00] Samir: interface endpoints typically use TLS on standard ports; we provide a short TCP/IP list. i'll attach a sample security group and required SG rules.
[05:08] Jared: egress IP ranges — we need stable IPs to allowlist for external vendor calls (only a few vendors). do you give static egress IPs?
[05:16] Samir: yes, for Private we can allocate fixed egress IPs via NAT in your account or advertise dedicated egress ranges — we'll coordinate with infra to lock these. Note: if you use our managed NAT in our account that can change on scaling; best is your NAT in your VPC.
[05:33] Maya: any compliance questions?
[05:35] Priya: SOC2 report and penetration test reports. also we need proof of data at rest encryption, and key separation.
[05:41] Maya: will share SOC2 + ISO + pentest summary. we do AES-256 at rest, TLS in transit, and support CMKs.
[05:49] Elena: are there any known limitations in eu-west-1 around GPU types / latency?
[05:54] Samir: good question — in eu-west-1 we typically run A10G and H100 instances depending on model; H100 availability can vary across zones which can affect tight latency SLOs. for strict p95 we'd design capacity across multiple AZs within eu-west-1 and consider reserved capacity (Dedicated) to guarantee throughput.
[06:13] Jared: what's the cost delta between hosted vs dedicated vs private? just rough order of magnitude?
[06:18] Maya: hosted lowest operational overhead but less isolation; cost per token can be higher at scale. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and reserved pricing — cheaper per token at commit. Private adds ops overhead (networking, infra) but gives control for compliance. i'll send a pricing snapshot tailored to your QPS after this call.
[06:34] Priya: we have strict data residency — no backups or logs to leave eu. can Redwood guarantee logs kept in region for private?
[06:40] Samir: yes, for Private we can keep logs and artifacts in-region and use your S3 buckets if needed. we'll include a diagram in the follow-up.
[06:50] Jared: for the pilot can you provide an IaC example? we use terraform 1.6 and modules.
[06:57] Samir: yes — sample terraform and modules for privatelink and TGW will be included in the repo I send.
[07:03] Maya: let's talk about fallbacks: if an AZ has capacity issues, will requests failover to another region?
[07:09] Samir: by default we failover to compatible model variants in the same region; cross-region failover is optional and must be approved for data residency. we can keep failover within eu-west-1 across AZs.
[07:21] Elena: and monitoring — do you expose token-level cost and latency per route?
[07:25] Maya: yes, Redwood Console has per-model and per-route dashboards, token breakdowns, traces. for Private we can forward metrics to your datadog/prometheus.
[07:35] Priya: what about key rotation for CMKs?
[07:38] Samir: rotation policies are customer-managed; we support seamless key rotation for encryption of artifacts as long as permissions are updated.
[07:44] Jared: any blockers you foresee for our pilot?
[07:47] Samir: none obvious — main tasks are: confirm region, provide NAT/egress diagram, and we run benchmarks. also confirm required retention for audit logs.
[07:58] Maya: ok quick recap and next steps — samir will run an egress/latency benchmark against eu-west-1 private nodes; maya will share security pack and pricing; jared will provide network diagrams and list of vendor IPs to allowlist; we'll schedule the networking deep dive for next week.
[08:18] Jared: sounds good, thanks team.
[08:21] Priya: thanks, looking forward to security docs.
[08:23] Elena: thanks all.

End of transcript.

References / Links mentioned: 
- Security pack (SOC2/ISO): https://redwood.example.com/security-pack
- Sample Terraform + IaC repo: https://drive.redwood.example.com/privatelink-samples (placeholder)
- Pricing snapshot (will be sent): note in follow-up deck

Call ended at 15:42 UTC.
